description: Team Banh Trang Tron is a 3-member team of high school students from FPT Tay Ha Noi. For the Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge, we are leveraging NASA Earth observation data to help farmers make data-driven decisions, adapt to climate shifts, and optimize agricultural practices.
summary: CropCast is a bilingual (Vietnamese and English) smart-farming companion that turns NASA Earth observation data into daily decisions for Vietnamese farmers. A farmer pins a field on a satellite map and enters the crop, variety, soil, and water source (for example ST25 rice or L14 peanut). CropCast then compares today’s conditions with 25 years of NASA data (2001-2026) for that exact location. It tells the farmer whether to water, wait for rain, drain, or watch for disease, and it explains why in plain language. It also estimates soil drainage from satellite data, recommends crop rotations, and shows a 12-month planting-risk calendar. Farmers observe the situation in the field with the actual conditions and enter the information into the website to receive advice on future farming strategies. Climate change is making Vietnam’s seasons less predictable, and most farmers can’t use raw satellite data. CropCast closes that gap, helping them cut water and fertilizer costs, protect their soil, and adapt with data instead of guesswork.
details:
What is it and how it works

CropCast is a bilingual (Vietnamese/English) smart farming app for farmers in Vietnam. Farmers enter their field location, crop and variety (for example, ST25 rice or L14 peanut), soil type, and water source. Every day, the app gives a clear “what to do today” recommendation: water the field, wait because rain is coming, open drainage ditches, or watch for leaf disease. Each recommendation includes a simple explanation.

Between seasons, CropCast shows a 12-month risk calendar (drought, flood, cold snaps) and suggests crop rotations based on the family’s goals, such as saving water, using less fertilizer, preventing pests, or earning extra income from livestock feed.

The app combines three sources of information:

NASA and climate data: NASA POWER (2001-2026), NASA Earthdata CMR satellite data (SMAP, MODIS, GRACE-FO, OCO-2), and greenhouse gas data from the US GHG Center.
Live forecasts: Open-Meteo gives current weather and a 7-day forecast for the exact field location. Esri satellite images help farmers find their plots.
Farmers’ own observations: Check-ins from the field help the app adjust its advice for each plot.

Main features:

Demo Mode with sample farms, no sign-up needed, and optional cloud sync with email or Google
Interactive Vietnam map with province and district selection
Daily task checklist (Done / Pending / Postpone)
Automatic soil drainage estimate using SMAP and GPM data
Field check-ins and PDF/CSV report export and import
25-year climate history and map layers
AI advisor that uses the field’s NASA data
Farmer forum by province or nationwide
Benefits
Personal advice: Recommendations match each field’s location, soil, and crop, so they are not generic.
Easy to use: Simple Mode uses color labels (Good / Needs Attention / Warning). Detailed Mode shows charts and satellite data.
Improves over time: Farmer check-ins make the advice more accurate.
Works with weak internet: Data is saved on the device for offline use.
Protects soil and saves money: Crop rotation, such as beans after rice, reduces pests, adds nitrogen, and lowers water and fertilizer costs.
Intended Impact

CropCast brings NASA Earth observation data to small farmers and turns it into daily decisions. We hope it will reduce water and fertilizer waste, give earlier warnings about drought, flood, cold, and disease, improve soil health, help farmers adapt to climate change, and encourage knowledge sharing through the forum.


How NASA Data Is Used
Home screen (“Why CropCast Recommends This”): NASA POWER Daily data (GWETTOP, GWETROOT, PRECTOTCORR) compares today’s conditions with 25 years of soil moisture records to explain watering and drainage advice.
My Fields (drainage estimate): NASA POWER, SMAP (SPL3SMP_E), and GPM data show how quickly topsoil dries after heavy rain, so the app can classify drainage as fast, moderate, or poor.
Season Planner: NASA POWER Monthly data (2001-2026) builds the 12-month risk calendar and scores crop rotation options.
Climate & NASA tab: NASA POWER, Earthdata CMR, and US GHG Center data provide charts, map layers, and Detailed Mode data from SMAP, MODIS (MOD13Q1), GRACE-FO, OCO-2, and EDGAR/GHGx.
AI Advisor: NASA baseline data for the field is added to the AI’s context, so answers use the real history of the plot.

Data sources and APIs: NASA POWER, NASA Earthdata CMR, US GHG Center (STAC API), Open-Meteo, Esri satellite imagery

Hardware: runs in a phone or computer browser; no special equipment needed


How it helps famers:
It turns complex satellite data into simple, one-line advice.
It estimates soil drainage automatically, so farmers do not need to guess.
It combines global satellite data with each farmer’s own observations.
Two modes serve both busy farmers and agricultural experts.
It uses the family’s goals in crop rotation planning.
It links greenhouse gas data, such as methane from flooded rice fields, to farming choices.
The AI advisor focuses only on farming and uses real field data.
Factors Considered
Language and literacy: full Vietnamese and English support with simple explanations
Connectivity: offline access and low mobile data use
Local needs: Vietnamese crop varieties, provinces and districts, and map pins limited to Vietnamese territory
Privacy: Demo Mode without sign-up, private cloud saving, and view links for family or co-ops
Transparency: clear information about where each NASA dataset is used
Sustainability: less water and chemical use, and better soil health
Usability: simple color labels, a task list, and quick switching between modes
